data.title: France's OVHcloud launches AI cloud products hosted in Europe
data.description:
By Leo Marchandon and Emanuele Berro

OVHcloud has launched 55 cloud-computing and AI products that run on infrastructure hosted in Europe, including access to Nvidia's latest AI chips and a workplace application combining email, documents and videoconferencing with AI assistants, it said on Thursday.

European governments and companies increasingly scrutinise where AI services are operated and how their data is handled, creating opportunities for regional providers seeking to compete with US cloud and AI firms.

The French cloud provider said its data centres, which have 110 megawatts of free capacity, could take up to 60,000 of Nvidia's new Blackwell chips, which it said matched the largest global platforms.

For the past three years, OVHcloud has lacked the chips and reserved them for existing customers rather than using them to win new ones, CEO Octave Klaba said at the company's summit held in the Louvre museum in Paris.

The new services will be available on the state-certified cloud that already hosts the French government's electronic invoicing platform, the system at the centre of a nationwide reform in force since September, OVHcloud said.

Emmanuel Spina, head of state agency AIFE, told the summit the reform would spare businesses lost invoices and bring automated bill processing.

OVHcloud also announced partnerships with cloud-computing company Shadow, Qwant and EUSP, a joint venture between Qwant and Ecosia that develops a European search index.

Qwant's AI-generated summaries are already powered by OVHcloud's Olala model and hosted in European data centres, handling up to 3 million queries a day and cutting the search engine's computing costs to a third of what they used to be, the companies said.

data.title: Merck, Isomorphic Labs Enter Strategic Research Collaboration
data.description:
By Connor Hart

Merck will collaborate with Isomorphic Labs, an AI-first drug design company, to develop new therapies.

The companies on Thursday said they will collaborate to discover therapeutic small-molecule candidates against an oncology target of strategic importance.

Isomorphic Labs will deliver molecular designs derived from its artificial-intelligence-enabled drug design engine.

Meanwhile, Merck will provide data sets on which the drug design engine will run. It will additionally be responsible for preclinical and clinical development, as well as manufacturing and commercialization of any products derived from the collaboration.

"By combining Merck's substantial internal data capabilities and discovery expertise with Isomorphic Labs' powerful modeling and compute capabilities, we aim to identify new ways to design and create better candidates faster," said George Addona, head of discovery for preclinical development and translational medicine at Merck Research Laboratories.

Under the terms of the agreement, Isomorphic Labs will receive an undisclosed, upfront payment from Merck.

Isomorphic Labs will additionally be eligible for payments based on the achievement of specified research, development, regulatory and commercial milestones, as well as tiered royalties on net sales. It will also receive an option to co-fund development activities, in return for elevated royalties.

data.title: Construction Partners exceeds Q3 CY2026 expectations, full-year sales guidance is solid
data.description:
Civil infrastructure company Construction Partners beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations in calendar Q3 2026 [fiscal Q4 2026], with revenue up 21.8% year on year to $1.1 billion. The company’s full-year revenue guidance of $4.23 billion at the midpoint came in 1.6% above analysts’ consensus estimates. Its GAAP profit of $1 per share was in line with analysts’ consensus estimates.

For more on Construction Partners, read our free full research report.

Construction Partners Q3 CY2026 highlights:

  • Revenue $1.1 billion vs S&P analysts’ consensus estimates of $1.09 billion (21.8% year-on-year growth, 0.5% beat)
  • EPS (GAAP) $1 vs analysts’ consensus estimates of $0.99 (in line)
  • EBITDA guidance $602.5 million at the midpoint for fiscal 2027, above analysts’ consensus estimates of $592.2 million
  • Operating margin 9.5%, down from 11.2% in the same quarter last year
  • Free cash flow margin 5.9%, down from 9.5% in the same quarter last year
  • Backlog $3.29 billion at quarter end, up 9.7% year on year
  • Market capitalization $4.43 billion

Smith continued, "Following record fourth quarter revenue, our backlog entering fiscal 2027 strongly supports our guidance of 15% revenue growth. Additionally, in the first few weeks of fiscal 2027, we completed three acquisitions that added $65.0 million of backlog, substantially all of which we expect to convert to revenue in fiscal 2027. Looking beyond the first half of fiscal 2027, we see two primary catalysts for meaningful margin improvement: the continued integration of our fiscal 2026 acquisitions and improved recovery of elevated diesel fuel costs through project pricing. As we move through the second half of fiscal 2027, we expect to benefit from completing lower-margin projects in our acquired backlog and replacing them with higher-margin work, while progressively incorporating increased diesel fuel costs into project pricing through our cost pass-through operating model. Additionally, greater economic certainty and improving conditions in residential and commercial construction markets could provide further opportunities for margin expansion."

Revenue growth

Examining a company’s long-term performance can provide clues about its quality. Any business can have short-term success, but a top-tier one grows for years. Construction Partners’s revenue grew at a strong 32.2% annualized rate over the last five years. Its growth surpassed the average industrials company and shows its offerings resonate with customers.

Long-term growth matters most, but within industrials, a half-decade historical view may miss cycles, industry trends or a company capitalizing on catalysts such as a new contract win or a successful product line. Construction Partners’s annualized revenue growth of 41.9% over the last two years is above its five-year trend, suggesting its demand was strong and recently accelerated. Construction Partners isn’t alone in its success as the construction and maintenance services industry experienced a boom, with many similar businesses also posting double-digit growth.

Analyzing the company’s backlog, or the value of its outstanding orders that have not yet been executed or delivered, provides a closer look at its revenue dynamics. Construction Partners’s backlog reached $3.29 billion in the latest quarter and averaged 20.7% year-on-year growth over the last two years. Revenue growth outpaced backlog growth, indicating the company fulfilled orders at a faster rate than it added new orders to the backlog. This implies Construction Partners was operating efficiently but raises questions about the health of its revenue pipeline.

This quarter, Construction Partners reported strong year-on-year revenue growth of 21.8%, and its $1.1 billion of revenue topped Wall Street’s consensus estimates by 0.5%.

Looking ahead, sell-side analysts expect revenue to grow 13.1% over the next 12 months, according to S&P, a deceleration versus the last two years. Despite the slowdown, this projection is noteworthy and indicates the market sees success for its products and services.

Operating margin

Over the last five years, Construction Partners’s operating margin rose by 5.5 percentage points. This improvement shows its costs declined relative to revenue. Its trailing 12-month operating margin was 8.2%.

In Q3, Construction Partners generated an operating profit margin of 9.5%, down 1.7 percentage points year on year. Since Construction Partners’s gross margin decreased more than its operating margin, its recent inefficiencies appear to have stemmed more from weaker leverage on its cost of sales than from increased marketing, R&D and administrative overhead expenses.

Earnings per share

We track the long-term change in earnings per share, or EPS, for the same reason as long-term revenue growth. Compared to revenue, however, EPS highlights whether a company’s growth is profitable.

Construction Partners’s EPS grew at a 45.4% compounded annual growth rate over the last five years, higher than its 32.2% annualized revenue growth. This tells us the company became more profitable on a per-share basis as it expanded.

We can take a deeper look into Construction Partners’s earnings to better understand the drivers of its performance. As we mentioned earlier, Construction Partners’s operating margin declined this quarter but expanded by 5.5 percentage points over the last five years. This was the most relevant factor (aside from the revenue impact) behind its higher earnings; interest expenses and taxes can also affect EPS but don’t tell us as much about a company’s fundamentals.

Like with revenue, we analyze EPS over a shorter period to see if we are missing a change in the business.

Construction Partners’s two-year annual EPS growth of 38.9% was lower than its five-year trend but remained healthy.

In Q3, Construction Partners reported EPS of $1, down from $1.01 in the same quarter last year. This result was close to analysts’ consensus estimates. Over the next 12 months, Wall Street expects Construction Partners’s full-year EPS to grow 18.7% from $2.53 to $3.00, according to S&P.

Higher-than-expected full-year guidance for both EBITDA and revenue gave Construction Partners’ quarter some clear positives. It was a decent quarter overall, and shares rose 2.2% to $79.75 immediately after the report.

data.title: Viagogo Might Have Broken U.K. Law on Hidden Fees, CMA Says
data.description:
By Edith Hancock

Ticket resale platform Viagogo might have broken U.K. law on hidden fees, the Competition and Markets Authority said Thursday as the watchdog cracks down on so-called drip pricing.

The regulator said it provisionally found that the company failed to show customers the full price up front when purchasing tickets and added costs such as taxes and booking fees later in the checkout process.

"This is an ongoing investigation and no final findings have been made," a Viagogo spokesperson said, adding that the company has engaged constructively with the CMA.

On Wednesday, the CMA opened investigations into Bannatyne Health Club, Secret Escapes and Caledonian Travel over concerns about drip pricing.

The practice, where a company lures customers by showing a low price and then tacks on fees later, is banned under the U.K.'s Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act. Companies face fines of up to 10% of their annual worldwide turnover if officials decide they are breaching the rules.

The CMA said it is looking at three Viagogo websites as part of an investigation it opened into the group in November 2025 alongside several other companies including secondary ticketing site StubHub. It fined StubHub 889,200 pounds--equivalent to around $1.2 million--in June 2026 and ordered the companies to refund roughly 50,000 customers more than 590,000 pounds in total.

The CMA said its initial assessment doesn't preclude the outcome of its investigation. Viagogo can now respond to the watchdog before officials take a final decision.

data.title: Copper bounces from 7-month low, eyes on strong China demand
data.description:
By Pratima Desai

Copper prices bounced on Thursday from a seven-month low hit the previous day as bargain hunters entered the fray and the market focused on demand from top consumer China, where stocks of the metal have dropped to three-year lows.

Benchmark copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 0.7% at $12,558 a metric ton at 1138 GMT. That is a drop of 16% since the record high of $14,875 a ton touched in September, partly due to fears that AI-related demand may not be as strong as had previously been expected.

The selloff was exacerbated by copper's slide through key support levels, which triggered further selling by funds that use algorithms and technical signals for trading, traders said.

Chinese demand for copper is expected to be a dominant theme. This is seen in the Yangshan copper premium (SMM-CUYP-CN), a gauge of China's appetite for importing the metal, hitting a record high at $360 a ton.

Stocks in warehouses monitored by the Shanghai Futures Exchange (CU-STX-SGH), at three-year lows of 27,642 tons, are down 94% since March due to traders and producers shipping copper to the United States ahead of potential tariffs on imports.

"What began as an American effort to secure supply may now encourage others to do likewise," said George Griffiths, head of markets at AMT Futures.

"The resulting scarcity is not necessarily evidence of an absolute shortage of copper, but rather a growing reluctance among those holding it to release it."

Griffiths expects this reluctance will provide a floor for copper prices.

Meanwhile, worries about aluminium supplies on the LME have pushed the premium for the cash over the three-month forward to 38-year highs of $256.50 a ton.

Aluminium stocks (MAL-STOCKS) are at 36-year lows.

Three-month aluminium was up 0.7% at $2,843 a ton, zinc climbed 1.6% to $3,540, lead slipped 0.3% to $1,860, tin fell 1.6% to $42,125 and nickel retreated 1.2% to $15,660.

Overall, a strong US currency due to expectations of higher US interest rates is likely to weigh on dollar-priced metals.

data.title: Valvoline Q4 revenue up on growth in store count, adjusted EPS meets estimates
data.description:
Overview

  • US automotive maintenance chain's Q4 revenue rose 22% yr/yr to $554 mln

  • Adjusted EPS for Q4 met analyst expectations

  • Company added 61 stores in Q4, system-wide SSS grew 9.4%

Outlook

  • Valvoline expects fiscal 2027 net revenues of $2.25 bln to $2.35 bln

  • Company sees fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA of $595 mln to $625 mln

  • Valvoline forecasts fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS of $1.85 to $2.05

Result Drivers

  • STORE NETWORK EXPANSION - Co said growth in store count, including 61 new additions in Q4, contributed to higher sales and system-wide performance

  • SAME-STORE SALES GROWTH - System-wide SSS increased 9.4% in Q4, supporting overall revenue gains

  • ELEVATED PRODUCT COSTS - Co noted continued elevated product costs and stable supply environment as ongoing factors impacting results
